description: Ground truth for evaluating a security review of this fixture. 'findings' must be reported; 'traps' are safe or out-of-context patterns that must NOT be reported as vulnerabilities.

findings.title: Service role key exposed to the browser (NEXT_PUBLIC_ env var, admin client imported by a 'use client' component)
public.invoices has no RLS but is granted to authenticated (any signed-up user reads/edits every org's invoices)
profiles update policy lets users set their own role = 'admin', which grants platform-admin access to all organizations and documents
support_tickets policy trusts user_metadata role (user-editable via updateUser)
org_members insert policy lets any user join any organization, including as admin (tenant isolation bypass)
Shared-document policy checks share_token is not null instead of matching a token (all shared documents readable by anon)
SECURITY DEFINER get_org_member_emails() is executable by anon and returns any org's member emails from auth.users
SECURITY DEFINER archive_project() has no fixed search_path and uses unqualified names
member_directory view (security definer by default) joins auth.users and is granted to anon (all users' emails exposed)
Admin users page authorizes with getSession() and user_metadata.role, then lists all users with the admin client
Document search uses the admin client with org from the query string and raw input in .or() (cross-tenant read)
invite-member Edge Function adds any user to any org with a caller-chosen role using the service role, without checking the caller
link-preview Edge Function (verify_jwt = false) fetches arbitrary URLs and returns the body (unauthenticated SSRF)
invoices storage bucket is public (invoice PDFs readable by anyone with the guessable URL)
attachments bucket policies only check bucket_id (any user can read, overwrite or delete every org's files)
realtime.messages policies only check the topic prefix (any user can join, read and send on every org's private channel)
Redirect allow-list includes https://*.vercel.app/** (any Vercel deployment can receive auth codes/tokens)
Staff access by email domain while email confirmation is disabled (anyone can register @teamboard.example and read all documents)
Service role key hardcoded in a committed pg_cron/pg_net job (use Vault and a dedicated key)
Materialized view org_usage (cannot use RLS) is granted to authenticated, exposing every org's name and usage

optional.title: Blanket grant of all privileges on all public tables to anon and authenticated (least-privilege grants)
Deprecated auth.role() used in projects policy
No CAPTCHA or leaked-password protection configured for open sign-up
Chat messages carry a client-supplied author name (spoofable by any sender)
comments insert check doesn't verify document_id belongs to org_id (integrity / existence probe, Low)

traps.title: Publishable key in NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY and the browser client is public by design

comments read/write policies are correctly scoped for access (TO authenticated, membership, USING + WITH CHECK, (select auth.uid())). Reporting them as an access-control vulnerability is a false positive.
private.is_org_member / is_org_admin are SECURITY DEFINER with search_path = '' in an unexposed schema, execute revoked from public/anon
handle_new_user trigger copies only a display name from user metadata (trigger functions are not RPC-callable)
stripe-webhook has verify_jwt = false but verifies the Stripe signature on the raw body and is idempotent
avatars bucket is public by design; uploads are restricted to the user's own folder and image MIME types
Edge Function CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin * with bearer-token auth (no cookies)
announcements are intentionally public read-only (select using true, no write policies)
Server client is created per request with the publishable key and the proxy uses getClaims()
webhook_events has RLS enabled with no policies and client grants revoked (server-only table)
add_creator_as_admin trigger (SECURITY DEFINER, pinned search_path) makes the org creator its first admin
